# Book I, Proposition 36

*Parallelograms on equal bases and in the same parallels are equal*

> Parallelograms which are on equal bases and in the same parallels are equal to one another.

<p align="center"><img src="../../figures/I/36-idea.svg" alt="Parallelograms on equal bases (red) and between the same parallels (blue) are equal (yellow), however differently they lean." width="420"></p>

<p align="center"><em>Parallelograms on equal bases (red) and between the same parallels (blue) are equal (yellow), however differently they lean.</em></p>

## Euclid's proof

<p align="center"><img src="../../figures/I/36.svg" alt="Euclid's figure for Proposition I.36, with Heath's letters" width="360"></p>

Let ABCD, EFGH be parallelograms which are on equal bases BC, FG and in the same parallels AH, BG;

I say that the parallelogram ABCD is equal to EFGH.

For let BE, CH be joined.

Then, since BC is equal to FG,

while FG is equal to EH,

BC is also equal to EH. [C.N. 1]

But they are also parallel.

And EB, HC join them;

but straight lines joining equal and parallel straight lines (at the extremities which are) in the same directions (respectively) are equal and parallel. [I. 33]

Therefore EBCH is a parallelogram. [I. 34]

And it is equal to ABCD;

for it has the same base BC with it, and is in the same parallels BC, AH with it. [I. 35]

For the same reason also EFGH is equal to the same EBCH; [I. 35]

so that the parallelogram ABCD is also equal to EFGH. [C.N. 1]

Therefore etc.

Q. E. D.

## In Lean

✅ Proved

From [`Elements/BookI/Prop36.lean`](../../Elements/BookI/Prop36.lean). Euclid's sentences are the `--` comments; the lines under each one are the Lean that carries it out.

```lean
/-- Parallelograms which are on equal bases and in the same parallels are equal to one another. -/
theorem Prop36 {A B C D E F G H : Point} (h₁ : Parallelogram A B C D) (h₂ : Parallelogram E F G H)
    (hbase : ‖B C‖ = ‖F G‖)
    (hAH : ∃ L : Line, OnLine A L ∧ OnLine D L ∧ OnLine E L ∧ OnLine H L)
    (hBG : ∃ L : Line, OnLine B L ∧ OnLine C L ∧ OnLine F L ∧ OnLine G L) :
    quadArea A B C D = quadArea E F G H := by
  -- Let ABCD, EFGH be parallelograms which are on equal bases BC, FG and in the same parallels
  -- AH, BG;
  obtain ⟨AH, hA, hD, hE, hH⟩ := hAH
  obtain ⟨BG, hB, hC, hF, hG⟩ := hBG
  have hpar : Parallel AH BG := (h₁.2.parallel hB hC hD hA).symm
  -- I say that the parallelogram ABCD is equal to EFGH.
  /- Euclid's case: EH runs the same way as BC, so C and H lie on one side of BE.
     We give his argument first, then turn the lettering round for the other case. -/
  have key : ∀ {E F G H : Point}, Parallelogram E F G H → ‖B C‖ = ‖F G‖ →
      OnLine E AH → OnLine H AH → OnLine F BG → OnLine G BG → SameSideOf C H B E →
      quadArea A B C D = quadArea E F G H := by
    intro E F G H h₂ hbase hE hH hF hG
    -- For let BE, CH be joined.
    /- The joining straight lines are named by their ends in I.33 below. -/
    -- Then, since BC is equal to FG,
    have hBC_FG : ‖B C‖ = ‖F G‖ := hbase
    -- while FG is equal to EH,
    have hEH : ‖E H‖ = ‖F G‖ := (Prop34 (A := E) (B := H) (C := F) (D := G) h₂).1
    -- BC is also equal to EH. [C.N. 1]
    have hBC_EH : ‖B C‖ = ‖E H‖ := CommonNotion1 hBC_FG hEH
    -- But they are also parallel.
    have hBCEH : AreParallel B C E H :=
      AreParallel.of_parallel h₁.2.1 h₂.2.2.1.symm hB hC hE hH hpar.symm
    -- And EB, HC join them;
    intro hdir
    -- but straight lines joining equal and parallel straight lines (at the extremities which
    -- are) in the same directions (respectively) are equal and parallel. [I. 33]
    have h33 := Prop33 hBCEH hBC_EH hdir
    -- Therefore EBCH is a parallelogram. [I. 34]
    /- Both pairs of opposite sides are parallel, which is the definition of a
       parallelogram. I.34 supplies FG = EH earlier in the argument. -/
    have hEBCH : Parallelogram E B C H :=
      ⟨h33.2.swap_left,
        AreParallel.of_parallel h₁.2.1 h₂.2.2.1 hB hC hH hE hpar.symm⟩
    -- And it is equal to ABCD;
    have e₁ : quadArea A B C D = quadArea E B C H := by
      -- for it has the same base BC with it, and is in the same parallels BC, AH with it. [I. 35]
      exact Prop35 h₁ hEBCH ⟨AH, hA, hD, hE, hH⟩
    -- For the same reason also EFGH is equal to the same EBCH; [I. 35]
    have harea : quadArea F E H G = quadArea B E H C :=
      Prop35 h₂.reverse.rotate.rotate.rotate hEBCH.reverse.rotate.rotate.rotate
        ⟨BG, hF, hG, hB, hC⟩
    /- This time the common base is EH. Book Zero turns both areas back to their
       given names, whichever diameter measures them. -/
    have e₂ : quadArea E F G H = quadArea E B C H := calc
      quadArea E F G H = quadArea F G H E := h₂.quadArea_rotate.symm
      _ = quadArea F E H G := (quadArea_reverse F G H E).symm
      _ = quadArea B E H C := harea
      _ = quadArea B C H E := quadArea_reverse B C H E
      _ = quadArea E B C H := hEBCH.quadArea_rotate
    -- so that the parallelogram ABCD is also equal to EFGH. [C.N. 1]
    exact CommonNotion1 e₁ e₂
  /- Book Zero settles which way EH runs. In the second case EFGH is read as
     HGFE, and the same argument applies without changing its area. -/
  have hEHBC : AreParallel E H B C :=
    AreParallel.of_parallel h₂.2.2.1.symm h₁.2.1 hE hH hB hC hpar
  have hequal : quadArea A B C D = quadArea E F G H := by
    rcases hEHBC.sameSideOf_or with hs | hs
    · exact key h₂ hbase hE hH hF hG hs.swap
    · rw [key h₂.reverse.rotate (hbase.trans (len_symm F G)) hH hE hG hF hs.swap,
        quadArea_reverse, quadArea_rotate₂, h₂.quadArea_rotate]
  -- Therefore etc.
  exact hequal
  -- Q. E. D.
```

## Mishnah

**A third parallelogram.** Euclid joins BE and CH, and EBCH is a parallelogram on the base BC with ABCD and on the base EH with EFGH. I.35 makes each given parallelogram equal to it, and Common Notion 1 makes them equal to each other. Euclid's bracket [I. 34] stands after "Therefore EBCH is a parallelogram", which in Lean is just the definition of `Parallelogram`, both pairs of opposite sides parallel. The Lean cites I.34 earlier, for FG equal to EH: that is what lets I.33 make EB and HC equal and parallel.

**Which way the letters run.** I.33 joins equal and parallel straight lines at the ends that are in the same directions, so C and H must lie on one side of BE (`SameSideOf`). Book Zero's `AreParallel.sameSideOf_or` says that they do, or else that E and C lie on one side of HB, which is the same thing with EFGH read as HGFE. So the Lean gives Euclid's argument once and uses it with either lettering. Each use of I.35 may fall in any of its cases: on the base EH, BC and FG may overlap or meet at an end. I.36 needs, then, the cases Heath reports Proclus adding under I.35 as well as Euclid's, and our `Prop35` proves them all. `quadArea_reverse` and `Parallelogram.quadArea_rotate` turn the areas back to their given names.

**The cases behind the picture.** Heath gives I.36 no note of its own. Among Heron's comments, though, he finds "Distinctions of a number of particular cases of Euclid's propositions according as the figure is drawn in one way or in another. Of this class are the different cases of I. 35, 36" (vol. 1, p. 22).

**What it rests on.** The Lean cites just Euclid's three brackets, with Common Notion 1. It draws neither BE nor CH, needing only their ends: Postulate 1 comes in through Book Zero, where `AreParallel.sameSideOf_or` settles which way EH runs and `Parallelogram.quadArea_rotate` measures a parallelogram by either diameter, and through all three citations. Each of them cites I.29, and Postulate 5 comes in through each.

**The modern way.** The area of ABCD is |(C − B) × (A − B)|, the length of BC times the distance between the parallels AH and BG. EFGH stands between the same parallels on a base FG equal to BC, and so has the same area.
